note: Adapted from the original English description of Haviland 1898 (originally Termes tenuior n. sp., later placed in Heterotermes); the alate (male and female) and the soldier are described, and the measurements are single values of the type specimens. In the OCR text "Wings 65 mm" and "1°6 mm" were restored from the context to 6.5 mm and 1.6 mm.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Published as a new species, Termes tenuior (later placed in Heterotermes). The alate is slender, dark brown above and paler below; the wings 6.5 mm long and 1.6 mm wide, hairy, the media lying between the submedia and the subcosta and reaching the wing tip unbranched; the soldier is 4 mm long, the head ochraceous yellow, the mandibles dark, the antennae 13-segmented.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Male body length 5 mm, slender, dark brown above (umbrinous) and pale below, the legs and antennae pale. Head short, oval, convex in lateral view; ocelli close to the compound eyes; fontanelle very indistinct; 4 indistinct pale spots forming a line almost level with the ocelli. Antennae 15-segmented, the second segment longer than the third, the rest gradually larger towards the tip. Postclypeus hardly protruding. Anterior margin of the pronotum slightly bilobed, the lateral margins converging rapidly, the posterior margin faintly lobed; posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum narrow. Forewing stubs much larger than the hindwing stubs, but not overlapping each other. Wings 6.5 mm long and 1.6 mm wide, hairy; a pale media lying between the submedia and the subcosta, running straight and unbranched to the wing tip; near the end of the subcosta the submedia becomes slender and reaches the wing tip, giving off about 11 branches. Hind leg not reaching the end of the abdomen. Abdomen slender, hairy; abdominal papillae present but minute. In the female the sternite of abdominal segment 7 is long, with a parabolic posterior margin.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body length 4 mm; mandibles dark, head ochraceous yellow, thorax and abdomen creamy white. Head 1.3 mm long and 0.8 mm wide, protruding above the antennal bases in lateral view. Antennae 13-segmented, the second segment longer or shorter than the third. Labrum lanceolate, acute, reaching the middle of the mandibles.
